# Bundled receive engine

This directory contains the native compiler inputs for the fldigi-web modem
adaptation, pinned to commit
`739174ecb182874ba595bafcd7ed5e8b4842a39e` of
[fldigi-web](https://github.com/crashdemons-external/fldigi-web).
The underlying fldigi version is 4.2.13. Its source archive identity is recorded
in `vendor/fldigi/SOURCE.json`.

The upstream source and generated overlay retain their original notices.
`PROVENANCE.json` maps each copied file to its source path and SHA-256.
`SOURCES.json` lists translation units for the native build.
The overlay was generated by upstream's `scripts/prepare-browser-core.py`.
The local `generated/include/emscripten/emscripten.h` defines only an empty
`EMSCRIPTEN_KEEPALIVE` macro. The application uses no Emscripten runtime.
The original generation scripts are retained for reference. Regeneration
requires the complete pinned upstream checkout.

The original RSID receiver, header, and mode assignments are also retained under
`vendor/fldigi/src/rsid` and `vendor/fldigi/src/include/rsid.h`. The Python
RSID receiver in `kiwiremote/rsid.py` adapts their Reed-Solomon symbol encoding
and FFT bucket matching for the application's four supported modes.

Run `python build_decoder.py` at the project root. The application-owned
receive-only entry point is `native/digital_decoder.cpp`. It accepts only
MFSK16, MFSK32, MFSK64, and Contestia 4-250 and emits received text.
The wider upstream native adaptation is retained to preserve its tested
interfaces. Those other modes and transmit functions are not exposed by the
application.

The adaptation and fldigi modem code use GPL-3.0-or-later. The FFT header
`gfft.h` uses LGPL-3.0-or-later. TINICONV retains its LGPL version 2 terms.
See `COPYING`, `COPYING.LESSER`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, the individual
source headers, and `web/licenses/tiniconv-*`. Original author information
is retained in `vendor/fldigi/AUTHORS`.

Distribute this corresponding source, the root build script and native entry
point with the application source for each release. The packaging spec includes
the applicable license texts and notices in the executable bundle.
